Background

The Buenos Aires Declaration on Trade and Women's Economic Empowerment, endorsed by 118 Members in the margins of MC11 in December 2017, led to the establishment of the Informal Working Group on Trade and Gender (IWG), in the WTO, September 2020, formally constituted under document WT/L/1095/rev.1. The IWG structures its technical work around four pillars: (1) Trade Policy Making & Experience Sharing, (2) Mainstreaming Gender in the WTO, (3) Reviewing Analytical Work, and (4) Aid for Trade.

IWG Work Pillars Show ▼
1 Trade Policy Making & Experience Sharing
IWG Members share best practices, information and exchange views on how to remove trade-related barriers and increasing the participation of women in trade. Under this pillar, they are specifically looking into gender-responsive trade policy making and gender-disaggregated data collection.
2 Mainstreaming Gender in the WTO
IWG Members consider and clarify what a 'gender lens' as a concept applied to international trade would entail and specifically consider how a gender lens could usefully be applied to the work of the WTO.
3 Reviewing Analytical Work
IWG Members review and discuss gender-related analytical work produced by the WTO Secretariat and other stakeholders.
4 Aid for Trade
Members explore how best to support the development and delivery of the gender-responsive Aid for Trade programmes.

Compendium Scope

The Informal Working Group on Trade and Gender (IWG): Achievements Tracking Compendium — Open Ended Since 2020 (WT/MIN(26)/25) maps and categorizes the work presented by members in the WTO Informal Working Group on Trade and Gender (IWG) since its establishment in September 2020. It centralizes, organizes and consolidates information on the gender-responsive policy initiatives designed and implemented by IWG members. The Compendium serves as a living reference tool, assisting policymakers, researchers, and practitioners to better understand how gender is integrated in trade policy — covering what members have presented, the policy instruments deployed, the outcomes sought, and the thematic areas addressed. Between 2020 and 2025, 187 technical presentations and policy dialogue sessions were delivered, centred around 17 core themes and showcasing 33 types of policy measures. The Compendium serves 4 key purposes.

Four Purposes of the Compendium
Capacity Building Tool
Facilitates learning and skill development for stakeholders engaged on trade and gender issues at the WTO
Knowledge Resource
Provides a comprehensive understanding of IWG work and its contribution to the WTO sustainable development agenda
Trade Policy Instrument
Showcases gender-responsive trade policy models across sectors and themes to guide governments
Archival Resource
Documents the history of the IWG, its evolution, major milestones, and contributions to gender equality in trade
